correctness.rationale: Integral weak Lefschetz (F dimension >=5, X dimension >=4) gives Pic(X)=Z^m and injects ambient degree-four cohomology. Primitive square-zero Picard classes are exactly +/- coordinate classes; nefness removes signs. Exact Koszul/Kunneth vanishings show each coordinate pencil is complete, giving a unique product-automorphism extension. Adjunction forces the multidegree stabilizer and the 1-dimensional (2,...,2) ideal piece forces preservation of F. All quantifiers and smoothness hypotheses are explicit. The embedded finite checker returned VERIFY_OK and is not treated as a universal proof.

originality.rationale: Direct reading of Quedo arXiv:2610.00709v1 Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 7.16 finds extension for scalar powers, notably all uniform d>2 Wehler sections; the final theorem excludes this known uniform case and includes primitive nonuniform canonical class (3,3,3,3,3,4). Product-of-projective-lines ambient Picard and unique Wehler recovery are not statements established by the compared single-projective-space complete intersection theorems. Indexed search and both own available ledgers returned no equivalent or dominating statement. An older general toric or multiprojective result is a genuine residual risk.
residual_risks: An older broad theorem on smooth ample complete intersections in toric or multiprojective varieties might implicitly imply this extension, although none was identified by alias and implication searches.

value.rationale: The 2026 Wehler result covers uniform polarizations only. The nonuniform and especially primitive-canonical cases form a motivated gap: arbitrary automorphisms of every smooth member are captured by a concrete intrinsic simultaneous stabilizer, obtained through square-zero integral classes, complete ruling pencils and the unique defining quadratic multidegree. This is a uniform structural automorphism classification across infinitely many natural general-type complete intersections, not a genericity assertion or a routine numerical increment.
